overview: Malaysia is a country in South-East Asia, made up of the southern part of the Malay Peninsula and the north of the island of Borneo. Its capital and largest city is Kuala Lumpur, home of the Petronas Towers. Malaysia became independent from the United Kingdom in 1957. It is a federation with an unusual monarchy: its king is chosen in turn from the rulers of nine states.

geography.text: Malaysia is split in two by the South China Sea. Peninsular Malaysia has mountains down the middle and coastal plains where most people live. On Borneo, the states of Sabah and Sarawak are covered in rainforest and include Mount Kinabalu, one of the highest mountains in South-East Asia. Malaysia's rainforests are among the oldest in the world.

history.text: Malacca was a great trading port in the 1400s, linking the Indian Ocean with China. It was taken by the Portuguese in 1511 and later by the Dutch and the British. Malaya became independent from Britain in 1957, and Malaysia was formed in 1963 together with Sabah, Sarawak and, for two years, Singapore.

events.title: Malacca Sultanate
events.text: Malacca is founded and grows into a major port.

events.title: British control
events.text: A treaty with the Dutch gives Britain control of Malacca.

events.title: Malaysia formed
events.text: Malaya, Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore form Malaysia.

government.text: Malaysia is a federal constitutional monarchy with a unique system: its king is chosen every five years from among the rulers of nine Malay states. The Prime Minister leads the government with the support of the elected House of Representatives.

economy.text: Malaysia is a major exporter of electronics and computer chips, palm oil, rubber and natural gas. The Petronas Twin Towers in Kuala Lumpur were the world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004.

culture.text: Malaysia is a mix of Malay, Chinese, Indian and Indigenous peoples, each with their own festivals, which are national holidays. Food such as nasi lemak and roti canai reflects this mix. The rainforests of Borneo are home to orangutans.

items.title: Nasi lemak
items.text: Rice cooked in coconut milk, the national dish.

items.title: Orangutans
items.text: Great apes found only in Borneo and Sumatra.

sport.text: Badminton is Malaysia's most successful sport, and Lee Chong Wei was world number one for years. Football is the most popular to watch. Sepang hosted Formula 1 races from 1999 to 2017 and still holds MotoGP.

items.title: Lee Chong Wei
items.text: Won three Olympic silver medals in badminton.

items.title: Sepang
items.text: A motorsport circuit near Kuala Lumpur.

didYouKnow: Malaysia's Petronas Towers were the world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004.
Rafflesia, a giant flower that smells of rotting meat, grows in Malaysia's rainforests.

keyPeople.name: Lee Chong Wei
keyPeople.text: World number one for nearly 200 weeks.

keyPeople.name: Michelle Yeoh
keyPeople.text: Won the Oscar for Best Actress in 2023.
